title: Walk the Golden Lane at Prague Castle
description: The largest ancient castle complex in the world by area, with St Vitus inside it and Kafka's sister's house on the lane.

title: Drink in a Czech pub where they pour a mliko
description: The Czechs drink more beer per head than anyone, and have four different pours of the same pilsner. Ask for one that is all foam.

title: See the bone chapel at Sedlec
description: Forty thousand skeletons arranged into a chandelier and a coat of arms by a woodcarver in 1870. An hour from Prague.

title: Drink the springs at Karlovy Vary
description: Twelve hot mineral springs drunk from spouted porcelain cups in a colonnade. They taste bad, which is held to be the point.

title: Descend into the Macocha abyss
description: A 138-metre sinkhole with a cave system beneath it that you leave by boat along an underground river.

title: Cycle the Lednice-Valtice cultural landscape
description: Two hundred square kilometres landscaped by one family over three centuries, with follies scattered through it and vineyards between.

title: Walk the Krakow main square and Wawel
description: The largest medieval square in Europe, with a trumpet call from the church tower every hour that breaks off mid-note.

title: Visit Auschwitz-Birkenau
description: Entry is free but must be booked, and a guided tour is strongly advised. Allow the whole day and expect it to be hard.

title: Go down into the Wieliczka salt mine
description: Three hundred and twenty-seven steps down to chapels, chandeliers and an entire cathedral carved out of rock salt by miners.

title: See how Warsaw rebuilt its old town
description: Eighty-five per cent destroyed in 1944 and rebuilt from Bellotto's paintings. World heritage listed for the reconstruction itself.

title: Understand the 1944 rising at its museum
description: Sixty-three days of fighting, two hundred thousand dead, and a city razed in reprisal. The museum does not soften any of it.

title: Walk the long market at Gdansk
description: A Hanseatic port rebuilt after the war, where the Second World War started and where Solidarity later began at the shipyard.

title: Sail the Masurian lakes
description: Two thousand connected lakes in the north-east, sailed rather than motored, with storks on every second chimney.

title: Walk to Sniezka on the Czech border
description: A 1,603-metre summit with a weather station like a flying saucer, and a border that runs straight through the top.

title: Soak at the Szechenyi thermal baths
description: Eighteen pools fed by two thermal springs, in a neo-baroque palace. The outdoor pool runs at 38 degrees through the snow.

title: Walk the Fisherman's Bastion at dawn
description: Seven turrets for the seven Magyar tribes, above the Danube and looking straight across at the parliament building.

title: Drink in a Budapest ruin bar
description: Derelict buildings in the old Jewish quarter filled with junk-shop furniture. Szimpla started it in 2002 and is still the template.

title: Take the shoe memorial on the Danube bank slowly
description: Sixty pairs of iron shoes for the Jews shot into the river by the Arrow Cross in 1944-45. No signage, and none needed.

title: Swim in Lake Balaton and the Heviz thermal lake
description: The largest biologically active thermal lake in the world, warm enough to swim in outdoors in January.

title: Taste aszu in a Tokaj cellar
description: Botrytised sweet wine aged in mould-lined cellars, made here since long before Sauternes and once the drink of kings.

title: Walk the old town and castle at Bratislava
description: A compact capital on the Danube, an hour from Vienna, with a castle on the hill and bronze statues climbing out of the pavement.

title: Walk to a Tatra mountain hut
description: The smallest alpine range in the world, packed into a strip you can cross in a day, with chamois and marmots on the scree.

title: Climb the ladders in Slovak Paradise
description: Gorges climbed on iron ladders and chains fixed into waterfalls, walked one way only because you cannot pass on them.

title: See Spis Castle from the ridge
description: One of the largest castle complexes in central Europe, four hectares of ruin on a limestone hill above the plain.

title: Row a pletna to the island on Lake Bled
description: A church on an island under a cliff castle. Ninety-nine steps up from the jetty, and tradition says the groom carries the bride.

title: Walk the Vintgar gorge boardwalk
description: A kilometre and a half of walkway pinned above the Radovna river, built in 1893 and still on the same alignment.

title: Raft the Soca river
description: Water an improbable turquoise from rock flour, through a valley that was the Isonzo front in the First World War.

title: Walk through the Skocjan caves
description: One of the largest underground canyons anywhere, crossed on a bridge forty-five metres above a river you can hear but not see.

title: Sit on the river in Ljubljana
description: A capital of three hundred thousand with a car-free centre, rebuilt around the river by one architect, Joze Plecnik.

title: Live inside Diocletian's Palace
description: A Roman emperor's retirement palace that a town moved into and never left. Three thousand people still live inside the walls.

title: Sail to the Pakleni islands from Hvar
description: A chain of wooded islets ten minutes off Hvar town, with coves that only fill up in the middle of August.

title: Hunt truffles in the Motovun forest
description: The largest white truffle ever recorded came out of this forest. Hilltop towns and Italian-influenced cooking around it.

title: Sit in the Pula amphitheatre
description: One of the six largest surviving Roman amphitheatres, and the only one with all four side towers still standing.

title: Listen to the sea organ at Zadar
description: Marble steps with pipes underneath, played by the waves. Hitchcock said Zadar had the best sunset in the world.

title: Walk the boardwalks at Krka
description: Travertine waterfalls in a river canyon, quieter than Plitvice and reachable by boat from Skradin.

title: Watch the rivers meet from Kalemegdan
description: A fortress fought over for two thousand years, above the point where the Sava runs into the Danube.

title: Go out on a Belgrade splav
description: Floating clubs moored along both rivers, running until dawn. The city's nightlife happens on the water.

title: Ride the Sargan Eight railway
description: A narrow-gauge line that loops in a figure of eight to climb the hill, rebuilt after decades derelict.

title: Climb to Petrovaradin fortress
description: The Gibraltar of the Danube, with sixteen kilometres of tunnel underneath and a clock whose hands are reversed for boatmen.

title: Watch the divers at Stari Most
description: An Ottoman bridge shelled to rubble in 1993 and rebuilt from the river stones. Local men still dive the twenty-four metres.

title: Walk the Sarajevo tunnel of hope
description: Eight hundred metres dug under the airport runway to supply a city under siege for 1,425 days. A section is preserved.

title: Drink Bosnian coffee in Bascarsija
description: Served in a dzezva with a cube of sugar held in the teeth, in an Ottoman bazaar where you can hear the call to prayer and church bells together.

title: Swim under the Kravica falls
description: A 25-metre horseshoe of falls on the Trebizat, with a swimmable pool at the base and far fewer people than Plitvice.

title: Climb the walls above Kotor
description: Thirteen hundred and fifty steps up the fortifications to San Giovanni, above a bay that behaves like a fjord.

title: Raft the Tara canyon
description: The deepest river canyon in Europe at 1,300 metres, on the edge of a national park of glacial lakes and limestone.

title: See Sveti Stefan from the coast road
description: A fifteenth-century fishing village on an islet, now a single hotel. The view from the road above is the free version.

title: Drive the Llogara pass to the Albanian Riviera
description: From a thousand metres of pine forest down to the Ionian in a series of hairpins, onto beaches that were closed to the world until 1991.

title: Walk the stone town of Gjirokaster
description: Ottoman tower houses with stone-slab roofs stacked up a hillside, and a cold war bunker museum under the castle.

title: See the thousand windows of Berat
description: White Ottoman houses layered up both sides of a gorge, with a castle at the top that people still live inside.

title: Take the Komani lake ferry to Valbona
description: A three-hour ferry through a flooded canyon to the Accursed Mountains, then a day's walk over the pass to Theth.

title: Swim in Lake Ohrid
description: One of the oldest and deepest lakes in Europe, three million years old, with endemic species found nowhere else.

title: Kayak the Matka canyon
description: A gorge half an hour from Skopje with ten caves, one of them the deepest underwater cave in the Balkans.

title: See Bran Castle and then the real Transylvania
description: Marketed as Dracula's castle on thin evidence. Worth it anyway, and the Saxon villages around Brasov are the actual reason to come.

title: Walk the Saxon fortified churches around Sibiu
description: Seven hundred years of German-speaking settlement left fortified churches in almost every village, several world heritage listed.

title: Drive the Transfagarasan
description: Ninety kilometres over the Fagaras mountains to 2,042 metres, built by Ceausescu at enormous cost. Snow closes it most of the year.

title: See the merry cemetery at Sapanta
description: Blue-painted grave markers carved with a rhyming verse about how each person actually lived, and often how they died.

title: Take a boat into the Danube Delta
description: Europe's best-preserved delta and its largest reed bed, with three hundred bird species and villages reachable only by water.

title: Tour the Palace of the Parliament
description: The heaviest building in the world, which cost a fifth of a country's GDP and flattened a sixth of the old city.

title: Walk to the Rila monastery frescoes
description: Founded in the tenth century and painted top to bottom in the nineteenth, in a valley two hours from Sofia.

title: Sit in the Roman theatre at Plovdiv
description: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in Europe, with a second-century theatre still used for concerts.

title: See the abandoned Buzludzha monument
description: A concrete flying saucer built for the Communist Party in 1981 and left to rot at 1,432 metres. Sealed, but visible up close.

title: Walk the Pirin lakes
description: Marble peaks and glacial lakes in a national park with the oldest tree in Bulgaria, a pine of thirteen hundred years.

title: Swim off the Black Sea coast at Sozopol
description: A Greek colony from the seventh century BC, now a wooden-housed old town on a peninsula with beaches either side.

title: Walk the bastions of Valletta
description: A whole capital built by the Knights of St John as a fortress in 1566, and small enough to cross in twenty minutes.

title: Book far ahead for the Hypogeum
description: A 5,000-year-old underground burial complex cut into rock. Eighty visitors a day, and tickets go months in advance.

title: Dive the Blue Hole at Dwejra
description: A natural rock chimney into the open sea. The Azure Window above it collapsed in 2017; the dive site is unaffected.

title: Walk Mdina after the day trippers leave
description: Called the silent city: three hundred residents inside a walled hill town where cars are almost entirely banned.

title: Walk to the Estanys de Tristaina
description: Three glacial lakes on a circular route at 2,300 metres, in a country that is mostly mountain above 2,000.

title: Soak at Caldea in Andorra
description: The largest thermal spa in southern Europe, fed by a sulphurous spring, under a glass spire in the middle of the capital.

title: Walk the Monaco Grand Prix circuit on foot
description: Three and a third kilometres of public road, including the tunnel and the hairpin, walkable any day the race is not on.

title: See the shark lagoon at the Oceanographic Museum
description: Built into a cliff face in 1910 and run for thirty years by Jacques Cousteau.

title: Walk between the three towers of San Marino
description: The oldest surviving sovereign state, on a limestone crag, with a path along the ridge linking its three fortresses.

title: Walk the Furstensteig ridge path
description: A cliff path with fixed cables above Vaduz, and the country's best-known walk. Sixteen kilometres of nation visible below.
